name: Where a spiral sweep is at step k
brief:
A survey drone sweeps a field of `rows` by `cols` plots in a clockwise spiral. It starts at the top-left plot `[0, 0]`, runs right along the top row, down the right edge, left along the bottom and up the left edge. It then does the same one ring further in, until it has visited every plot once. Step 1 is the first plot.

Write `spiral_cells(rows, cols, ks)`, which returns, for each step number `k` in `ks`, the plot `[row, col]` visited at step `k`, with rows and columns counted from 0 at the top left.

Example. For a field of 3 rows and 4 columns, the sweep visits `[0, 0]`, `[0, 1]`, `[0, 2]`, `[0, 3]`, `[1, 3]`, `[2, 3]`, `[2, 2]`, `[2, 1]`, `[2, 0]`, `[1, 0]`, `[1, 1]` and `[1, 2]`. So `spiral_cells(3, 4, [5, 11, 12])` returns `[[1, 3], [1, 1], [1, 2]]`.
constraints: $O(\log(\min(\text{rows}, \text{cols})))$ work a step is the target. A field can have $5 \times 10^8$ rings, so even skipping ring by ring is too slow.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: The rings before ring `t` cover every plot outside the inner field of `rows - 2t` by `cols - 2t`, so their count is a difference of two areas. Binary search for the ring holding step `k`, then place the step on that ring's top, right, bottom or left side.

examples.note: Steps 11 and 12 are the inner ring, which is a single row of two plots.
A field one plot wide is a single column, swept from the top down.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. The obvious method walks the spiral a step at a time, which takes up to $10^{18}$ steps, and skipping whole rings one by one, with or without sorting the steps first, still takes $5 \times 10^8$ rings. The step to the target is a binary search on the ring, since the plots outside ring `t` are `rows * cols - (rows - 2t) * (cols - 2t)`. The change from listing the spiral is that only chosen steps are wanted, on a field far too large to list.
notes: The plots before ring `t` grow with `t`, so the ring holding step `k` is the largest `t` with fewer than `k` plots before it.
An inner ring of one row or one column is just its top side, or its right side after the first plot, which the same four cases cover.
Each step costs a binary search over at most $5 \times 10^8$ rings, about 30 rounds, so the work is $O(q \log(\min(\text{rows}, \text{cols})))$.

planted.slip: Counting the steps from 0 shifts every answer one plot along the spiral.
Going down the left edge first sweeps the spiral anticlockwise.
Swapping the ring's height and width is right only on a square field.
Walking the spiral a step at a time takes up to $10^{18}$ steps.
Skipping one ring at a time for each step still takes $5 \times 10^8$ rings on a large field.
Sorting the steps and skipping rings once for all of them still walks $5 \times 10^8$ rings.
